candidates.statement: Assume that the polynomial hierarchy does not collapse. Then there exists a sampling problem that can be solved eﬃciently on a quantum computer and that is provably hard for classical randomized algorithms.

There exists a classical algorithm that takes as input an irrep λ of the symmetric group Sn, a permuta- tion g ∈Sn, and outputs an integer k(g) such that k(g) = χλ(g) for at least a 1 −1/n100 fraction of permutations g ∈Sn. The algorithm has runtime nO(log n).

candidates.statement: There exists a constant B > 0 such that the fraction of permutations g ∈Sn with c(g) > B log (n) cycles is at most 1/n100 for all large enough n. If c(g) ≤B log n, use the MPS algorithm to compute χλ(g), which takes time nO(log n). Otherwise, if c(g) > B log n, output some ﬁxed integer (say zero). This gives the desired algorithm. ■ Next let us consider the row sampling problem.
